member.summary: Reads the types a console line is usually spelled in.

remarks.para: Every type it knows is a single row of a table, each with a reader of its own. A type missing from the table is visible as a missing row - which a chain of conditions never made it, and which is how and went unread for a while.

Numbers are read with the invariant culture and with the number styles spelled out, on purpose. A command typed into a console is not a document: a build running under a comma-decimal locale must not read 1.5 differently, and 1,5 must be refused rather than taken for fifteen - which is what a thousands separator allowed by default would make of it. That is also why the table is not .

Dates are read by whatever the runtime reads under the invariant culture - an ISO date with or without its time, a month spelled by name, a time alone meaning today. Numeric dates are read month first, so 21.09.2026 is refused, but 01.02.2026 is the second of January; a date that has to be read the same by everyone is best written the ISO way.

Enums are the one kind that cannot be a row, as there is one per enum type. They are read by the names of their members, ignoring the case the way the rest of the input is matched - and never by a number, which would let a value the enum does not declare slip through. Anything else is left to a converter of the game's own.
